title: APAO: Bridging the Training-Inference Gap in Generative Recommendation via Adaptive Prefix-Aware Optimization

problem.claim: Generative recommendation predicts the next item through autoregressive token generation conditioned on user interaction histories.

gap.claim: Token-level likelihood training assumes ground-truth tokens are available, whereas beam-search inference can prematurely discard the correct item when its prefixes receive low scores, creating a training-inference inconsistency.

contributions.claim: The authors propose Adaptive Prefix-Aware Optimization, a framework that introduces prefix-level optimization losses to align training with inference.
The authors design an adaptive worst-prefix optimization strategy that dynamically focuses training on the most vulnerable prefixes under beam-search constraints.
The framework includes theoretical analyses of its effectiveness and efficiency.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that APAO consistently alleviates the training-inference inconsistency.
The authors report improved performance across generative recommendation backbones.

narrative_sequence.summary: Generative recommendation is presented as an emerging paradigm that formulates sequential recommendation as autoregressive next-item generation.
Existing token-level training and beam-search inference are described as inconsistent because low-scoring prefixes can eliminate the correct item.
APAO addresses the inconsistency with prefix-level losses and adaptive optimization of vulnerable prefixes.
The authors report theoretical analyses and broad performance improvements across generative recommendation backbones.

source_observation.claim: When training exposes only ground-truth token paths but inference prunes prefixes, optimizing vulnerable prefixes may better match the inference-time failure mode.

interpretation.claim: Training objectives for autoregressive ranking systems may need to account for search-path survival, not only token-level likelihood.

application.claim: For systems that generate ranked candidates through beam search, evaluate or optimize prefix retention under the intended decoding constraints.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond the reported generative recommendation backbones and beam-search setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative effect sizes.
The theoretical results and assumptions are not detailed.
The abstract does not describe the exact prefix-level losses or adaptive optimization procedure.
